title: Unauthenticated semantic requests can choose an arbitrary user_id
reasoning: Both semantic routes use the authenticated identity when present, but silently fall back to the caller-supplied request.user_id when no identity is available. The models only validate the shape of user_id, not authorization. If these routes are reachable without an authenticated install identity, a client can request summarization or title generation under another user's session/config by supplying that user_id, because the resolved_user_id is passed into the session-backed service path.
recommendation: Require an authenticated install identity for these routes, or enforce an explicit local-only trust boundary before accepting request.user_id. If unauthenticated fallback is required for tests or single-user local mode, gate it behind a clearly named configuration flag and reject arbitrary user_id values otherwise.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for authentication fallback or user_id spoofing behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests where get_current_authenticated_install_identity returns None and request.user_id names a different/valid user; assert the request is rejected unless an explicit local unauthenticated mode is enabled.
